question: Does the iCloud adapter serialize independent read-only folder requests behind its session mutex, and can bounded concurrent reads remove that queue without changing authentication ownership?
arms: current adapter: two synthetic folder HTTP requests held until both arrive
adapter with read-only session forks and a four-request account limit: same fixture
endpoint: Both HTTP requests reach the fixture before either response is released; record whether the pre-fix regression fails and the post-fix test passes. No network service or live mount is part of this synthetic control.
prediction: The current adapter times out because it holds one mutex through network I/O. A shared-cookie read-only session fork lets both reach the fixture while a semaphore bounds account concurrency to four.
scope: Synthetic transport control only. The installed Cirrove daemon and isolated iCloud validation mount remain untouched. Live latency and Apple acceptance require separate evidence.

results.pre_fix: The filtered regression executed one test and failed after its two-second deadline: the second HTTP request could not reach the fixture while the first held the session mutex awaiting a response.
results.post_fix: The same filtered test executed one test and passed in 0.04 seconds. Both requests reached the fixture before either response was released.
results.interpretation: This demonstrates removal of the adapter's per-account network serialization for two synthetic directory reads. It does not measure an Apple endpoint, file-manager crawl, or provider rate limits; the four-request cap is conservative pending live measurement.
